display_name: Tyrrell's Vat 1 Semillon, New South Wales
raw_content:
{
  "hook": "Hunter Valley Semillon is the only white that starts life as a lean, 11.5 % abv lemon-squeeze and ends up a honeyed, toast-laden 20-year stunner—Tyrrell’s Vat 1 is the reference point for the transformation.",
  "wine_summary": "Tyrrell’s has made Vat 1 every vintage since 1963 from their Short Flat and HVD blocks on the alluvial delta of the Hunter River. These own-rooted, dry-farmed vines sit in friable sandy loam over alkaline clay that traps just enough moisture to keep the berries small and the acids sky-high. The resulting wine is picked at 10.5–11 % potential alcohol, ferments in 70-year-old 2 700 L baltic-pine vats with ambient yeast, sees zero oak, and is bottled early to lock in its battery-acid freshness. Ten years later it blossoms into toast, beeswax and roasted lemon—an Australian signature that costs a quarter of white Burgundy with comparable age-worthiness.",
  "terroir_expression": "The Hunter’s subtropical heat is cancelled out by night irrigation from the nearby Brokenback Range; diurnal shift can hit 15 °C, preserving Semillon’s razor acidity. Sandy topsoil drains quickly, forcing roots to the alkaline clay sub-layer that doles out magnesium and potassium—minerals that translate into the wine’s waxy mid-palate and saline finish. Black silty loam holds just enough water to avoid hydric stress, so the berries stay thin-skinned and high in tartaric acid, the structural backbone that allows 30-year cellaring.",
  "vinification_summary": "Whole-bunch pressing keeps pH around 2.9; juice settles 24 h, then ferments at 14 °C for six weeks in 120-year-old 2 700 L Kaluga vats—thick staves that give micro-oxygenation without oak flavour. The wine is racked twice, sulphured to 35 ppm free SO₂, and bottled five months after harvest while still turbid with fine lees; this early bottling is critical to capturing the reductive thiol profile (mercaptans) that later polymerise into honey and toast.",
  "food_pairing": [
    "Sydney rock oysters with mignonette—razor acidity cuts brine and mirrors oyster liquor.",
    "Nashville hot chicken—lemon and lanolin tame chili heat while acid refreshes the palate.",
    "Whole snapper steamed with ginger and spring onion—delicate flesh needs low alcohol, citrus lift lifts aromatics.",
    "Aged Comté 24 months—emerging toast in both wine and cheese create seamless resonance.",
    "Fine dining: butter-poached lobster with lemon beurre blanc—wine’s future beeswax notes echo nutty brown butter."
  ],
  "comparable_wines": [
    "Mount Pleasant Elizabeth Semillon — same Hunter terroir, slightly earlier picked, lighter body, 30 % lower price.",
    "Château Coutet ‘Les Demoiselles’ Barsac — same thiol-driven toast evolution, but botrytis adds sweetness and silk.",
    "Trimbach Cuvée Frédéric Emile Riesling — similar acid spine and toast development, though Riesling shows petrol instead of beeswax."
  ],
  "style_profile": "Medium-bodied dry white with electric acidity and a time-release toast-honey evolution.",
  "cellar_recommendation": "Drink 2016–2046; cork prefers 12 °C constant, 70 % humidity, lay bottles horizontal to keep natural cork swollen.",
  "value_assessment": "USD 60 lands you a 20-year white that competes with $90 Chablis Premier Cru and $120 aged Sancerre. No other region delivers this transformation at the price; it’s a cellar steal.",
  "market_position": "You’ll spot Vat 1 on Sydney fine-dining lists at AUD 140 and in serious Australian sections of Manhattan retailers. Somms use it to teach Semillon ageworthiness; collectors buy half-cases for 10-year spacing.",
  "insider_take": "Most drinkers open Hunter Semillon too young and complain it’s thin—wait ten years and the same bottle tastes like grand cru white Burgundy at half the tariff. If you need instant gratification, spend the money elsewhere.",
  "aging_potential_years": 30,
  "drinking_window_min_years": 8,
  "drinking_window_max_years": 30,

  }
}

parsed.wine_summary: Tyrrell’s has made Vat 1 every vintage since 1963 from their Short Flat and HVD blocks on the alluvial delta of the Hunter River. The resulting wine is picked at 10.5–11 % potential alcohol, ferments in 70-year-old 2 700 L baltic-pine vats with ambient yeast, sees zero oak, and is bottled early to lock in its battery-acid freshness. Ten years later it blossoms into toast, beeswax and roasted lemon—an Australian signature that costs a quarter of white Burgundy with comparable age-worthiness.
parsed.terroir_expression: The Hunter’s subtropical heat is cancelled out by night irrigation from the nearby Brokenback Range; diurnal shift can hit 15 °C, preserving Semillon’s razor acidity. Black silty loam holds just enough water to avoid hydric stress, so the berries stay thin-skinned and high in tartaric acid, the structural backbone that allows 30-year cellaring.
